newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euroshares end down, hit by Wall St, politics.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euroshares end down, hit by Wall St, politics.

text.p: European bourses ended the day well down on Friday with investors worried about political uncertainties in Britain and France, and unsettled by a poor performance on Wall Street.

On currency markets, the dollar perked up against the mark and strengthened against the yen in late trade. It had weakened against the yen for most of the session as the suspension of a major Japanese insurer prompted speculation about higher interest rates in Tokyo.

London and Paris, both facing general elections in coming weeks, made moderate losses at the close but Frankfurt suffered the most, its computerised IBIS index tumbling over one percent in final trading.
"It's the end of the week, everyone's tired and wants to go home," said a dealer in London.

A weak showing on Wall Street -- it was down 0.75 percent as Europe closed -- and strong British first quarter growth figures depressed London prices and added to concerns over near-term interest rate rises.

London's FTSE index ended with losses of 0.43 percent amid a background of doubt over the outcome of May 1 elections in which the Conservative government is expected to be ousted by the opposition Labour party, according to opinion polls.
Dealers and strategists said Friday morning's GDP figures added more weight to the case for higher near-term interest rates. A rate rise soon after the poll is anticipated whoever comes to power.

"The figures mean four percent annualised growth which is pretty strong growth, well above trend and reinforces the likelihood of rate increases soon," said Credit Lyonnais Laing economist, Andrew Smith.
The Paris bourse made hefty losses in thin morning trade with many investors holding back amid election uncertainty, but recovered some poise to finish down only a few points.
"We're waiting for the polls and for the election," one broker said. "The polls are being closely watched but they have a very short term impact.
An IPSOS poll showing the ruling conservative coalition would get a wafer-thin majority weighed on the French financial markets.

"Investors will steer clear until the election. The risk, in terms of market valuation, is too great. Better wait a month and find out what France's direction will be," said one trader. "Until then, we'll be driven by the polls."

Frankfurt had the worst day. Floor trade ended down 0.6 percent but dealings in the after-hours computerised IBIS index fell by 1.15 percent at the finish as investors pocketed profits before the weekend.

Market interest focused on the construction sector after builders Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG both said they were pulling out of Germany's high-speed rail Transrapid project because of questions about the project's costs.
In currencies, more buoyant dollar sentiment pulled the U.S. currency above 1.72 marks towards the end of the session and helped it on the yen.

Traders said the dollar had been nudged down a bit too far for comfort against the yen and mark this week despite its underlying strength, and that position adjustment was going ahead before this wekend's meeting of finance ministers from the G7 industrialised countries.
"The dollar was looking a bit oversold and we'd taken out a very short-term downtrend," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives trading at the Cooperative Bank in London.
"Now that we've broken out of that trend, we're heading towards the 1.7250-marks area," Beauchamp said.

The mark had gained on other European currencies because of renewed worries over European monetary union and next month's French elections, and this had led to selling of European currencies against the dollar as well, they said.

"When there's nervousness over EMU the market tends to sell European currencies for marks. But it seems they're selling them against the dollar as well today, since they want both dollars and marks ahead of the G7," said one trader at a U.S. bank here.
The dollar recovered against the yen after earlier weakness over anxiety about a rise in Japanese market interest rates overnight because of renewed worries over Japan's financial industry.

The anxiety was prompted by the suspension of the big Japanese insurance company Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Company. This triggered concern that Nissan's foreign bonds would be liquidated, causing a large repatriation of funds.
STOCKS
London's FTSE 100 ended down 18.8 points at 4,369.7.
The Paris CAC-40 index closed down 3.37 points at 2536.26.
Frankfurt's DAX finished down 23.26 at 3,374.10.
CURRENCIES
The dollar stood at 1.7256 against the mark in late trade versus 1.7150 on Thursday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.10 from 125.90.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $342.50 an ounce after ending at $340.65 in
London on Thursday. Silver was at $4.73, one cent higher.
